cohort: Prairie vole pups delivered either via cesarean or vaginal delivery were cross-fostered and studied throughout development into adulthood.
finding: Cesarean-delivered prairie voles failed to form partner preferences in adulthood, a deficit that could be normalized by oxytocin treatment at delivery, and also showed minor differences in regional oxytocin receptor expression and gut microbial composition and development.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery in prairie voles was associated with altered vocalizations, less cohesive group huddling, reduced heat shedding, and a deficit in partner-preference formation in adulthood, with minor differences in oxytocin receptor expression and gut microbial composition.
